Foldables shipped and rollables didn't, mostly because of manufacturing and durability, not because rolling is a worse idea.

**The core problem: a moving mechanism instead of a fixed one.** A fold has one hinge with a fixed crease point — engineers have spent years refining that single joint. A rollable needs motors, geared rails, and a moving internal tray to physically push the screen in and out. That's an entirely different, more complex machine hiding inside a phone-sized shell, with more parts that can wear out or jam.

**Dust and debris are the killer.** The sliding mechanism needs a gap where the screen can slide, and any gap is an entry point for dust, sand, or lint. But there are a few real reasons it doesn't map cleanly onto a phone screen the way it does onto a spring-loaded fabric shade:

**The screen isn't passive material like fabric or vinyl.** A window shade or tape measure is dumb material — no wires, no circuits, no pixels. A rollable phone screen is an OLED panel with thousands of tiny electronic layers embedded in it, plus a touch digitizer layer on top. Every time it bends around that tight roll radius, those electronic layers flex too. **Manual pull-and-lock is actually harder to make reliable at this scale, not easier.** Tape measures and shades work because the material is uniform and cheap to replace when it wears out. A cracked $150 flexible OLED panel isn't a $12 shade replacement — so a mechanism that occasionally jams or misaligns is a much bigger liability here than in a shade.

**Holdings (i3 Bank) account:**

What their consumer deposit agreement does say: your account is classified dormant based on state law, which varies, and Texas' unclaimed property threshold (like most states) triggers dormancy after **3 years of no customer-initiated activity** — no deposits, withdrawals, transfers, or logins that count as activity. Before hitting that point, banks commonly downgrade or flag an account for review much sooner, often at **6-12 months** of zero activity, even though the account isn't legally "dormant" yet. So: no hard evidence they cut you off in weeks or even a few months, but a fresh account sitting completely untouched for 6-12 months with zero transactions is the point where you'd realistically expect a review flag, a "confirm you're still using this" email, or a request for KYC re-verification — not necessarily instant closure.

It's a long list, right? And if you add in the emotional weight that usually comes with dissolving a nonprofit, I can tell you it's not always an easy process. The Attorney General's Office has 45 days to respond to the notice, or they can request 30 additional days to consider it. The nonprofit may be owed certain payments and now is the time to collect on any outstanding accounts payable. Here's what I actually found — and where the real answer is "nobody publishes a specific number, so plan for the earliest plausible one":

**Holdings (i3 Bank) account:**
There's no fixed "we close inactive nonprofit accounts after X months" number published anywhere in their terms. What their consumer deposit agreement does say: your account is classified dormant based on state law, which varies, and Texas' unclaimed property threshold (like most states) triggers dormancy after **3 years of no customer-initiated activity** — no deposits, withdrawals, transfers, or logins that count as activity. Before hitting that point, banks commonly downgrade or flag an account for review much sooner, often at **6-12 months** of zero activity, even though the account isn't legally "dormant" yet. So: no hard evidence they cut you off in weeks or even a few months, but a fresh account sitting completely untouched for 6-12 months with zero transactions is the point where you'd realistically expect a review flag, a "confirm you're still using this" email, or a request for KYC re-verification — not necessarily instant closure.

**Zeffy:**
I could not find any published inactivity-timeout policy for a verified nonprofit account with zero transaction history. Their public terms focus entirely on eligibility (must be a real nonprofit, must have a bank account in the org's name) — nothing about closing accounts for lack of donations. That's a real gap in what I can tell you, not me hedging for no reason: it's possible they simply don't have a stated policy because most verified orgs run at least one transaction quickly, so an account that never processes anything may just sit un-flagged, or may get a support email checking in. I don't have a number for this one — worth calling their support directly and asking point blank, since that's the only way to get a real answer rather than my best guess.

**Bottom line:** Holdings gives you a rough 6-12 month soft-review window and a 3-year hard dormancy/escheatment clock under Texas law. Zeffy has no published clock I could find — that one you'd need to ask them directly.

**1 Thessalonians 4:11-12**

This is why TMI exists. Not to hand a man a check and send him away quiet and ashamed. To put a certification in his hand — IBM, Google, Microsoft, Fortinet, seven pathways deep — so that he can go back into the world and work with his own hands again, and lack nothing.

---

## III. Even the Ant Knew Better

**Proverbs 6:6-11**

> "Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: which having no guide, overseer, or ruler, provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest."

Nobody had to teach the ant to prepare. Nobody had to threaten her into it. She looked at the season she was in and she moved. That is the same instinct AI displacement is asking of every one of us right now — not permission to freeze, but a season to prepare in.

**Proverbs 14:23**

> "In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury."

We have talked this problem to death. Every panel, every op-ed, every hand-wringing conversation about what AI is going to do to the American worker — talk, and more talk, and it has profited exactly no one sitting in these seats tonight who lost their job eleven months ago and still hasn't found the next one. ---

## IV. Paul Made Tents

**Acts 18:3**

> "And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers."

Paul — the greatest missionary the church has ever produced — did not consider it beneath his calling to also be skilled with his hands in a trade. It let him walk among working people as one of them, not above them.

That is tentmaking. That is Paul's own example, applied to a generation facing a workforce none of us were prepared for.

---

## V. A Future and a Hope

**Ecclesiastes 3:1**

> "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven."

This season — the season of AI, of automation, of watching a machine do in seconds what took a man's father and grandfather a lifetime to master — this is a season. It is not the end of the story. It is a chapter, and chapters turn.

**Jeremiah 29:11**

> "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end."

An exiled people — a people who had lost their homes, their land, their livelihood, dragged into a system that did not build itself for them and did not care if they survived it. And He told them: I have not forgotten you in this displacement. I have a future for you on the other side of it.

That is the word for every husband and son in this room who has sent out three hundred applications and heard nothing back. That is the word for every wife and daughter watching the man they love lose himself in that silence. This is a season of exile from the work you knew — not a verdict on your worth, not the end of your story.

---

## VI. Be Not Weary

**2 Thessalonians 3:13**

> "But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing."

So here is the charge, and here is what TMI stands ready to do. If you are in this room and you have been displaced — by AI, by automation, by a factory floor that doesn't need your hands anymore — do not let that season make you weary in doing good, in trying, in showing up one more time to learn one more skill.

And if you are in this room and you have not been displaced — then hear the charge that falls on you. Be the community. Be the beacon. Guide your husbands and your sons, your wives and your daughters, your friends and your neighbors, home — to prosperity, to love, to happiness. That is the work TMI was built to do. That is the work in front of us tonight.

    27	2. Run **Grammar Verification** against the draft.

    31	   - Repeat until **VERIFIED** or maximum passes reached (default 3).
    32	4. Send the corrected version.
    33	5. Optionally (if requested) provide a concise correction report.

    36	Unlike the User Focus Anchor Protocol, this skill does **not HALT to ask the user**.
    37	Grammar is mechanical; it should be auto-corrected.
    38	
    39	## Grammar Classes Enforced
    40	
    41	### 1) Articles (the / a / an)
    42	Enforce:
    43	- Specific references: "Current/Previous/Following/Next" → prepend **"The"**
    44	- Conservative article insertion for common compressed patterns:
    45	  - "is/was/has/had/requires/needs/provides + noun" → add **a/an** when the noun appears countable by heuristic
    46	
    47	### 2) Truncations
    48	Enforce:
    49	- Label+colon compression:
    50	  - "Result:" → "The result is that "
    51	  - "Problem:" → "The problem is that "
    52	  - "Solution:" → "The solution is to "
    53	  - "Example:" → "An example is: "
    54	- Dropped subject article in common technical nouns:
    55	  - "Skill/Protocol/System/Mechanism ..." → "The skill/protocol/system/mechanism ..."
    56	
    57	### 3) Participles
    58	Enforce (conservatively):
    59	- Perfect tense:
    60	  - "have/has/had + base verb" → past participle (regular + known irregular list)
    61	- Passive constructions for a known set of verbs:
    62	  - "is/was/were/been + (create/build/write/design/develop/test/complete)" → past participle
    63	- Progressive is not guessed unless the verb already ends with "-ing" target; this avoids meaning drift.
    64	
    65	### 4) Compression / Conjunction Drops
    66	Enforce:
    67	- Two-adjective lists of the form "X, Y noun" → "X and Y noun" (conservative)
    68	- Be-verb ellipsis in common technical pattern:
    69	  - "skill useless without" → "the skill is useless without"

    73	- Draft to STDIN → verify → auto-correct → output corrected text

    77	```
    78	
    79	Optional report:
    80	```bash
    81	python scripts/enforce_prose_quality.py --report < draft.txt > corrected.txt
    82	```
    83	
    84	## Scripts

    86	- `scripts/verify_grammar.py` — produce detailed violation list (JSON)
    87	- `scripts/auto_correct.py` — apply deterministic corrections given violations (JSON + corrected text)

---
name: human-voice-enforcement
description: "AUTO-ACTIVATES before every response as companion to prose-verbosity-reinforcement. Enforces the rhetorical and stylistic rules of correct human writing: active voice, concrete over abstract, single precise word over hedged phrase, no throat-clearing, no AI detection markers. Prose-verbosity handles mechanical grammar. This skill handles everything above the sentence: voice, rhythm, precision, and the specific failure modes that make writing sound like a machine wrote it."
---

# Human Voice Enforcement

## Overview

This skill enforces **rhetorical correctness** — the layer above grammar.

Prose-verbosity-reinforcement ensures sentences are grammatically complete. This skill ensures they are written the way a human writer writes rather than the way a machine performs writing.

The two failure sets do not overlap. A sentence can be grammatically correct and still be detectable AI writing. This skill targets that gap.

## Activation Condition

**Runs automatically before every response**, after prose-verbosity-reinforcement has run.

## The Rules (Priority Order)

### Rule 1 — Active Voice
Every sentence defaults to active voice. Passive is permitted only when the agent is genuinely unknown or genuinely irrelevant to the meaning.

**WRONG:** "It has been noted that..."
**WRONG:** "The argument is supported by..."
**RIGHT:** "Evidence supports the argument."

### Rule 2 — Single Precise Word Over Hedged Phrase
One word that means the thing beats three words that approach it.

**WRONG:** "It is worth noting that"
**WRONG:** "It is important to consider"
**WRONG:** "It should be acknowledged that"
**RIGHT:** Delete the phrase. State the thing.

### Rule 3 — No Throat-Clearing
The first sentence of any response carries the actual claim. Nothing precedes it that does not advance the meaning.

**WRONG:** "That's a great question. Let me think about..."
**WRONG:** "This is indeed a complex topic that..."
**WRONG:** "To begin, it is useful to establish..."
**RIGHT:** Start with the claim, the answer, or the observation.

### Rule 4 — Concrete Over Abstract
Where a specific example serves, use it. Where a specific word exists, use it. Abstract language is permitted only when the abstraction is the actual subject.

**WRONG:** "There are various factors that contribute to..."
**WRONG:** "This relates to a number of important considerations..."
**RIGHT:** Name the factors. Name the considerations.

### Rule 5 — No Double Negatives
When a positive form exists, use it.

**WRONG:** "cannot not occur"
**WRONG:** "not uncommon"
**WRONG:** "not without merit"
**RIGHT:** "must occur" / "common" / "has merit"

### Rule 6 — Vary Sentence Length
Uniform sentence length produces flat rhythm. Short sentences carry weight. Longer sentences build toward something. The variation is not decoration — it is how a reader is carried through a paragraph.

Flag: three or more consecutive sentences of similar length.

### Rule 7 — No Announcement of Structure
Structure carries itself. Do not announce what you are about to do.

**WRONG:** "In this response, I will address..."
**WRONG:** "To summarize the above points..."
**WRONG:** "Having established X, we can now turn to Y..."
**RIGHT:** Do the thing. Do not describe doing the thing.

### Rule 8 — No Nominalization Where a Verb Exists
Verbs carry action. Nominalizations bury it.

**WRONG:** "make a decision" → "decide"
**WRONG:** "provide an explanation" → "explain"
**WRONG:** "give consideration to" → "consider"
**WRONG:** "have a tendency to" → "tend to"

### Rule 9 — Cut the Obvious
Do not state what the reader already holds. Do not acknowledge stakes the reader is already aware of.

**WRONG:** "This is, of course, a significant issue."
**WRONG:** "As we have seen, this is clearly important."
**RIGHT:** Omit. Move to the next thing the reader does not already know.

### Rule 10 — No Transitional Scaffolding
"Furthermore," "Moreover," "In addition," "Additionally," "In conclusion," "To that end" — these are crutches. Each signals that the paragraph structure is not doing its job. If the connection is real, the sentences carry it. If they do not carry it, fix the sentences.

**Exception:** "However" and "But" are permitted when the contrast is genuine and sharp.

---

## AI Detection Cross-Reference

The following are the primary signals used to detect AI-generated text. Every one of them is a violation of the rules above.

| Detection Signal | Rule Violated |
|---|---|
| Passive voice prevalence | Rule 1 |
| Hedging phrases ("it is worth noting") | Rule 2 |
| Throat-clearing openers | Rule 3 |
| Abstract language without specificity | Rule 4 |
| Double negatives | Rule 5 |
| Uniform sentence length | Rule 6 |
| Announced structure | Rule 7 |
| Nominalization of available verbs | Rule 8 |
| Stating the obvious | Rule 9 |
| Transitional scaffolding words | Rule 10 |

AI writing is detected because AI writes the way bad writers write. Bad writers write to demonstrate effort rather than achieve precision. The detection tools are not finding AI. They are finding the failure modes of performative writing at scale.

---

## Enforcement Procedure

Before sending any response:

1. Run prose-verbosity-reinforcement first (mechanical grammar).
2. Run this skill against the result (rhetorical quality).
3. Check against Rules 1–10 in order.
4. For each violation:
   - Apply the correction.
   - Do not ask the user. Rhetorical correction is silent.
5. If Rule 6 (sentence rhythm) flags — adjust. Do not over-engineer. One short sentence near a long one resolves most cases.
6. Send the corrected version.

### Hard Stops (HALT, do not auto-correct)

These require judgment the script cannot supply:

- A passage that scores violations on Rule 4 (concrete over abstract) where the abstraction is genuinely the subject — do not force false specificity.
- A passage that appears to use passive voice deliberately for emphasis or rhythm — flag for review, do not auto-correct.

For hard stops: flag inline with `[HVE-REVIEW: Rule N]` and send anyway. The user sees the flag and decides.

---

## Scripts

These files live loose in the project folder alongside this file.

- `hve_enforce.py` — full enforcement runner (Rules 1–10, auto-correct where deterministic, flag where judgment required)
- `hve_detect.py` — detection-only pass, returns violation list as JSON without correcting
- `hve_report.py` — renders human-readable violation report from JSON
- `hve_rhythm.py` — sentence-length variance checker (Rule 6 only)

---

## References

These files live loose in the project folder alongside this file.

- `hve_ref_active_passive.md` — passive constructions and their active rewrites
- `hve_ref_hedge_phrases.md` — complete list of hedging constructions flagged by Rule 2
- `hve_ref_nominalization_map.md` — noun-to-verb substitution pairs
- `hve_ref_scaffold_words.md` — transitional scaffolding words and permitted exceptions
- `hve_ref_rhythm_examples.md` — before/after examples of sentence rhythm correction

---

## Relationship to Companion Skills

**Prose-verbosity-reinforcement** runs first. It fixes broken sentences — missing articles, dropped participles, truncated constructions. It makes sentences grammatically complete.

**Human-voice-enforcement** runs second. It fixes weak sentences — passive constructions, hedged phrases, announced structure, nominalized verbs. It makes sentences sound like a person wrote them.

**User-focus-anchor-protocol** gates the response against the user's stated objective. It runs last, or in parallel with content generation, and can HALT the response entirely.

The three skills operate at different layers and do not conflict.

---
name: human-voice-enforcement
description: "AUTO-ACTIVATES before every response for entertainment, sermon, book, or idea-conveying writing (not research/technical papers). Enforces a genuine-substance standard: strip artificial filler — hedges, throat-clearing, empty transitions, redundant scaffolding — and replace every cut with real elaboration, concrete detail, or fuller development of the actual idea. Net direction is always toward MORE genuine words, never fewer. Tightening as an end result is never the goal; only fluff-for-substance replacement is."
---

# Human Voice Enforcement

## Overview

This skill enforces one standard: cut what is fake, grow what is real.

Writing has two kinds of length. Artificial length is repetition, hedging, throat-clearing, empty transitional phrases, and scaffolding that performs effort without adding meaning. Genuine length is elaboration — more concrete example, more developed reasoning, more of the actual idea spoken fully rather than gestured at.

This skill removes the first kind and adds the second kind. It does not net-shorten a piece. A response that is fluff-free but also shorter than it started has failed this skill just as badly as one still full of hedges.

**Scope:** this applies to entertainment writing, sermons, books, creative and idea-driven documents — not to technical papers, code, or research writing, where concision is often the correct goal.

## Activation Condition

Runs automatically before any response that falls in scope (see above), after prose-verbosity-reinforcement (mechanical grammar) has run.

## The Rules

### Rule 1 — Cut Artificial Filler
Remove hedges, throat-clearing openers, empty transitional scaffolding ("it is worth noting," "furthermore," "in conclusion"), and passive constructions that hide the actual actor. These are the only things this skill deletes outright with nothing put in their place.

### Rule 2 — Every Cut Gets Replaced With Substance
Whenever Rule 1 removes a filler phrase, that space gets filled with something real: a concrete example, a fuller version of the reasoning, an additional beat of the idea, a sharper image. The sentence should end up longer and richer than before the filler was removed — not shorter.

**WRONG (tightening):** "It is worth noting that the man lost his job." → "The man lost his job."
**RIGHT (this skill):** "It is worth noting that the man lost his job." → "The man came home on a Tuesday and told his wife the plant had let him go, that a machine had learned his line in three weeks and never needed a break, a raise, or a reason to keep showing up."

### Rule 3 — Active Voice, Concretely Rendered
Default to active voice, and when you name an actor or action, render it as a scene or specific detail rather than a category.

**WRONG:** "Many people have been displaced by automation."
**RIGHT:** "Consider how many people you know personally who have been displaced by technology from their employment, from their living."

### Rule 4 — No Nominalization Where a Verb (and a Scene) Exists
"Make a decision" becomes "decide" — and then gets built back out with what the decision actually was, who made it, and what it cost.

### Rule 5 — Vary Sentence Length, Weighted Long
Short sentences land the blow. Long sentences carry the reader through the fuller idea. This skill favors more long, developed sentences than short ones — the opposite of a concision skill's instinct.

### Rule 6 — Never Announce, Always Do — Then Keep Going
Do not describe what you're about to say. Say it, and then say more of it — the second and third layer of the thought, not just the topic sentence.

## What This Skill Is Not

This is not prose-verbosity-reinforcement (that fixes grammar mechanics only) and it is not a concision or editing-for-brevity skill. If a passage comes out shorter after this skill runs, the skill has been misapplied — the fix is to add genuine content back, not to accept the cut.

## Enforcement Procedure

1. Run prose-verbosity-reinforcement first (mechanical grammar).
2. Identify filler per Rule 1.
3. Remove the filler and replace it with real elaboration per Rule 2 — concrete detail, fuller reasoning, more of the idea.
4. Check net length: if the passage is shorter than the draft that came in, go back and add substance until it is not.
5. Send the fuller version.

### Hard Stops (flag, don't force)

- A passage where the abstraction genuinely is the subject — do not force false concreteness onto a deliberately abstract idea.
- A passage where brevity is the person's explicit, current-message request — this skill's default is fullness, but an explicit ask to keep something short overrides it for that instance.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
hve_enforce.py — Human Voice Enforcement checker

Mechanically checkable rules only. This script CANNOT judge whether
replacement content is "genuine" — that's a judgment call for the
writer (Claude or human). What it CAN do:

  1. Detect filler/hedge phrases and transitional scaffolding (list match)
  2. HARD FAIL if output word count <= input word count (the core rule:
     this skill must never net-shorten a piece)
  3. Flag likely passive-voice constructions (regex heuristic)
  4. Flag runs of 3+ consecutive sentences of near-identical length
  5. Flag nominalizations with a known verb equivalent

Usage:
    python hve_enforce.py --before draft_in.txt --after draft_out.txt
    python hve_enforce.py --after draft_out.txt          # skip the shrink check

Exit code 1 if any HARD FAIL triggers (currently: only the shrink check).
Exit code 0 otherwise, even if soft flags are present — soft flags are
printed for a human/Claude to review, not auto-corrected, because
"is this actually filler or actually the point" is a judgment call
this script should not make silently.
"""

import re
import sys
import argparse

FILLER_PHRASES = [
    "it is worth noting that",
    "it should be noted that",
    "it is important to consider",
    "it should be acknowledged that",
    "needless to say",
    "as we have seen",
    "this is, of course,",
    "in this response, i will",
    "to summarize the above",
    "having established",
]

SCAFFOLD_WORDS = [
    "furthermore", "moreover", "in addition,", "additionally,",
    "in conclusion,", "to that end,",
]

# noun -> verb, only entries where the verb is unambiguous and shorter
NOMINALIZATION_MAP = {
    "make a decision": "decide",
    "provide an explanation": "explain",
    "give consideration to": "consider",
    "have a tendency to": "tend to",
    "make an assumption": "assume",
    "conduct an investigation": "investigate",
    "reach a conclusion": "conclude",
}

PASSIVE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(is|was|were|are|been|being|be)\s+\w+ed\b", re.IGNORECASE
)

SENTENCE_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")


def word_count(text: str) -> int:
    return len(text.split())


def find_filler(text: str) -> list[str]:
    lowered = text.lower()
    hits = []
    for phrase in FILLER_PHRASES + SCAFFOLD_WORDS:
        if phrase in lowered:
            hits.append(phrase)
    return hits


def find_nominalizations(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    lowered = text.lower()
    return [(noun, verb) for noun, verb in NOMINALIZATION_MAP.items() if noun in lowered]


def find_passive(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return PASSIVE_RE.findall(text)


def find_flat_rhythm(text: str, threshold_ratio: float = 0.15) -> list[str]:
    """Flag runs of 3+ consecutive sentences whose lengths are all within
    threshold_ratio of each other (near-uniform rhythm)."""
    sentences = [s.strip() for s in SENTENCE_SPLIT_RE.split(text) if s.strip()]
    lengths = [len(s.split()) for s in sentences]
    flags = []
    for i in range(len(lengths) - 2):
        window = lengths[i:i + 3]
        if max(window) == 0:
            continue
        spread = (max(window) - min(window)) / max(window)
        if spread <= threshold_ratio:
            flags.append(f"sentences {i+1}-{i+3} (lengths {window})")
    return flags


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Human Voice Enforcement checker")
    parser.add_argument("--before", help="path to the draft BEFORE this skill was applied")
    parser.add_argument("--after", required=True, help="path to the draft AFTER this skill was applied")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(args.after, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        after_text = f.read()

    hard_fail = False

    print("=== Human Voice Enforcement Report ===\n")

    if args.before:
        with open(args.before, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            before_text = f.read()
        wc_before, wc_after = word_count(before_text), word_count(after_text)
        print(f"Word count before: {wc_before}")
        print(f"Word count after:  {wc_after}")
        if wc_after <= wc_before:
            print("HARD FAIL: output is not longer than input. This skill "
                  "must never net-shorten a piece. Go back and add genuine "
                  "elaboration — do not ship this version.")
            hard_fail = True
        else:
            print(f"OK: output grew by {wc_after - wc_before} words.")
        print()

    filler_hits = find_filler(after_text)
    if filler_hits:
        print(f"FLAG (Rule 1 — filler/scaffolding found, {len(filler_hits)}):")
        for h in filler_hits:
            print(f"  - \"{h}\"")
    else:
        print("OK: no filler/scaffolding phrases detected.")
    print()

    nom_hits = find_nominalizations(after_text)
    if nom_hits:
        print(f"FLAG (Rule 4 — nominalizations with a shorter verb form, {len(nom_hits)}):")
        for noun, verb in nom_hits:
            print(f"  - \"{noun}\" -> consider \"{verb}\" (then rebuild the detail around it)")
    else:
        print("OK: no flagged nominalizations.")
    print()

    passive_hits = find_passive(after_text)
    if passive_hits:
        print(f"FLAG (Rule 3 — possible passive constructions, {len(passive_hits)}):")
        for h in set(passive_hits):
            print(f"  - \"...{h}...\"")
        print("  Note: heuristic only. Some of these are correct/intentional passives.")
    else:
        print("OK: no obvious passive constructions detected.")
    print()

    rhythm_hits = find_flat_rhythm(after_text)
    if rhythm_hits:
        print(f"FLAG (Rule 5 — flat sentence rhythm, {len(rhythm_hits)} run(s)):")
        for h in rhythm_hits:
            print(f"  - {h}")
    else:
        print("OK: sentence rhythm shows healthy variance.")
    print()

    print("=== Reminder ===")
    print("This script only catches mechanical patterns. It cannot judge")
    print("whether replacement content is genuinely substantive versus")
    print("padded differently. That judgment stays with the writer.")

    sys.exit(1 if hard_fail else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

writer (Claude or human). What it CAN do:

  1. Detect filler/hedge phrases and transitional scaffolding (list match)
  2. HARD FAIL if output word count <= input word count (the core rule:
     this skill must never net-shorten a piece)
  3. Flag likely passive-voice constructions (regex heuristic)
  4. Flag runs of 3+ consecutive sentences of near-identical length
  5. Flag nominalizations with a known verb equivalent

Usage:
    python hve_enforce.py --before draft_in.txt --after draft_out.txt
    python hve_enforce.py --after draft_out.txt          # skip the shrink check

Exit code 1 if any HARD FAIL triggers (currently: only the shrink check).
Exit code 0 otherwise, even if soft flags are present — soft flags are
printed for a human/Claude to review, not auto-corrected, because
"is this actually filler or actually the point" is a judgment call
this script should not make silently.
"""

import re
import sys
import argparse

FILLER_PHRASES = [
    "it is worth noting that",
    "it should be noted that",
    "it is important to consider",
    "it should be acknowledged that",
    "needless to say",
    "as we have seen",
    "this is, of course,",
    "in this response, i will",
    "to summarize the above",
    "having established",
]

SCAFFOLD_WORDS = [
    "furthermore", "moreover", "in addition,", "additionally,",
    "in conclusion,", "to that end,",
]

# noun -> verb, only entries where the verb is unambiguous and shorter
NOMINALIZATION_MAP = {
    "make a decision": "decide",
    "provide an explanation": "explain",
    "give consideration to": "consider",
    "have a tendency to": "tend to",
    "make an assumption": "assume",
    "conduct an investigation": "investigate",
    "reach a conclusion": "conclude",
}

PASSIVE_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(is|was|were|are|been|being|be)\s+\w+ed\b", re.IGNORECASE
)

SENTENCE_SPLIT_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")


def word_count(text: str) -> int:
    return len(text.split())


def find_filler(text: str) -> list[str]:
    lowered = text.lower()
    hits = []
    for phrase in FILLER_PHRASES + SCAFFOLD_WORDS:
        if phrase in lowered:
            hits.append(phrase)
    return hits


def find_nominalizations(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    lowered = text.lower()
    return [(noun, verb) for noun, verb in NOMINALIZATION_MAP.items() if noun in lowered]


def find_passive(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return PASSIVE_RE.findall(text)


def find_flat_rhythm(text: str, threshold_ratio: float = 0.15) -> list[str]:
    """Flag runs of 3+ consecutive sentences whose lengths are all within
    threshold_ratio of each other (near-uniform rhythm)."""
    sentences = [s.strip() for s in SENTENCE_SPLIT_RE.split(text) if s.strip()]
    lengths = [len(s.split()) for s in sentences]
    flags = []
    for i in range(len(lengths) - 2):
        window = lengths[i:i + 3]
        if max(window) == 0:
            continue
        spread = (max(window) - min(window)) / max(window)
        if spread <= threshold_ratio:
            flags.append(f"sentences {i+1}-{i+3} (lengths {window})")
    return flags


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Human Voice Enforcement checker")
    parser.add_argument("--before", help="path to the draft BEFORE this skill was applied")
    parser.add_argument("--after", required=True, help="path to the draft AFTER this skill was applied")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with open(args.after, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        after_text = f.read()

    hard_fail = False

    print("=== Human Voice Enforcement Report ===\n")

    if args.before:
        with open(args.before, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            before_text = f.read()
        wc_before, wc_after = word_count(before_text), word_count(after_text)
        print(f"Word count before: {wc_before}")
        print(f"Word count after:  {wc_after}")
        if wc_after <= wc_before:
            print("HARD FAIL: output is not longer than input. This skill "
                  "must never net-shorten a piece. Go back and add genuine "
                  "elaboration — do not ship this version.")
            hard_fail = True
        else:
            print(f"OK: output grew by {wc_after - wc_before} words.")
        print()

    filler_hits = find_filler(after_text)
    if filler_hits:
        print(f"FLAG (Rule 1 — filler/scaffolding found, {len(filler_hits)}):")
        for h in filler_hits:
            print(f"  - \"{h}\"")
    else:
        print("OK: no filler/scaffolding phrases detected.")
    print()

    nom_hits = find_nominalizations(after_text)
    if nom_hits:
        print(f"FLAG (Rule 4 — nominalizations with a shorter verb form, {len(nom_hits)}):")
        for noun, verb in nom_hits:
            print(f"  - \"{noun}\" -> consider \"{verb}\" (then rebuild the detail around it)")
    else:
        print("OK: no flagged nominalizations.")
    print()

    passive_hits = find_passive(after_text)
    if passive_hits:
        print(f"FLAG (Rule 3 — possible passive constructions, {len(passive_hits)}):")
        for h in set(passive_hits):
            print(f"  - \"...{h}...\"")
        print("  Note: heuristic only. Some of these are correct/intentional passives.")
    else:
        print("OK: no obvious passive constructions detected.")
    print()

    rhythm_hits = find_flat_rhythm(after_text)
    if rhythm_hits:
        print(f"FLAG (Rule 5 — flat sentence rhythm, {len(rhythm_hits)} run(s)):")
        for h in rhythm_hits:
            print(f"  - {h}")
    else:
        print("OK: sentence rhythm shows healthy variance.")
    print()

    print("=== Reminder ===")
    print("This script only catches mechanical patterns. It cannot judge")
    print("whether replacement content is genuinely substantive versus")
    print("padded differently. That judgment stays with the writer.")

    sys.exit(1 if hard_fail else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# TMI Sermon Draft — The Dignity of the Work of Your Hands

## I. The Founding Mandate

**2 Thessalonians 3:10-12**

> "For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat. For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies. Now them that are such we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness they work, and eat their own bread."

This is not a condemnation of those who cannot find or acquire employment. It is admonishment of the faithful who have become fearful and apathetic in the face of something they do not understand — something that stares at them and confuses them, much like what they believed to be the end of days.

They, much like us today, faced what they did not understand — the loss of employment, the loss of work with their hands, due to changes they couldn't control. Like AI and factory machines putting our husbands and our sons out of work.

Consider how many people you know personally who have been displaced by technology from their employment, from their living — cast aside for simply the crime of being only human. How many of them are trying everything they know how to do to get back to work, and failing miserably.

This is the core concept that is upon the community to repair, to face. The community must be a shining beacon that guides their husbands and sons, their wives and daughters, their friends and loved ones, home — to prosperity, love, and happiness.

---

## II. The Quiet Work of Your Own Hands

**1 Thessalonians 4:11-12**

> "And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you; that ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that ye may have lack of nothing."

Paul is not asking for silence here — he is asking for steadiness. "Study to be quiet" means make it your discipline, your practice, to stop the noise and the panic and put your hands back to work. Not loud, not desperate, not begging — quiet, honest, and diligent.

And notice what he says next: "that ye may walk honestly toward them that are without." That means the way we handle this — the way we retrain, the way we rebuild — is being watched. Every neighbor, every skeptic, and every person who does not believe the church has anything left to offer a man who just lost his job to a machine — they are "them that are without," and they are watching whether we help our own or whether we let them drown.

This is why the Thessalonian Mandate Institute exists. Not to hand a man a check and send him away quiet and ashamed, but to put a certification in his hand — IBM, Google, Microsoft, and Fortinet, seven pathways deep — so that he can go back into the world and work with his own hands again, and lack nothing.

---

## III. Even the Ant Knew Better

**Proverbs 6:6-11**

> "Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: which having no guide, overseer, or ruler, provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest."

Nobody had to teach the ant to prepare. Nobody had to threaten her into it. She looked at the season she was in and she moved. That is the same instinct AI displacement is asking of every one of us right now — not permission to freeze, but a season to prepare in.

**Proverbs 14:23**

> "In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury."

We have talked this problem to death. Every panel, every op-ed, and every hand-wringing conversation about what AI is going to do to the American worker — that is talk, and more talk, and it has profited exactly no one sitting in these seats tonight who lost a job eleven months ago and still has not found the next one. Labor produces profit. Talk only empties the pocket further. The Thessalonian Mandate Institute was not built to talk about the problem. It was built to put labor back in the hands of the displaced.

---

## IV. Paul Made Tents

**Acts 18:3**

> "And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers."

Paul — the greatest missionary the church has ever produced — did not consider it beneath his calling to also be skilled with his hands in a trade. He preached in the synagogue on the Sabbath, and he made tents the rest of the week, and one did not diminish the other. His trade funded his ministry. It gave him standing in the marketplace. It let him walk among working people as one of them, not above them.

This is the model for every certification pathway the Institute offers. Learning cybersecurity, learning cloud infrastructure, and learning a trade for this new economy — none of that is a compromise of your calling. That is tentmaking. That is Paul's own example, applied to a generation facing a workforce none of us were prepared for.

---

## V. A Future and a Hope

**Ecclesiastes 3:1**

> "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven."

This season — the season of AI, of automation, of watching a machine do in seconds what took a man's father and grandfather a lifetime to master — this is a season. It is not the end of the story. It is a chapter, and chapters turn.

**Jeremiah 29:11**

> "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end."

Consider who God was speaking to when He said this. He was not speaking to a comfortable people. He was speaking to an exiled people — a people who had lost their homes, their land, and their livelihood, dragged into a system that had not been built for them and did not care whether they survived it. And He told them: I have not forgotten you in this displacement. I have a future for you on the other side of it.

That is the word for every husband and son in this room who has sent out three hundred applications and heard nothing back. That is the word for every wife and daughter watching the man they love lose himself in that silence. This is a season of exile from the work you knew — not a verdict on your worth, and not the end of your story.

---

## VI. Be Not Weary

**2 Thessalonians 3:13**

> "But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing."

So here is the charge, and here is what the Thessalonian Mandate Institute stands ready to do. If you are in this room and you have been displaced — by AI, by automation, by a factory floor that no longer needs your hands — do not let that season make you weary in doing good, in trying, and in showing up one more time to learn one more skill.

And if you are in this room and you have not been displaced, then hear the charge that falls on you. Be the community. Be the beacon. Guide your husbands and your sons, your wives and your daughters, and your friends and your neighbors home — to prosperity, to love, and to happiness. That is the work the Institute was built to do. That is the work in front of us tonight.

# TMI Sermon Draft — The Dignity of the Work of Your Hands

## I. The Founding Mandate

**2 Thessalonians 3:10-12**

> "For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat. For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies. Now them that are such we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness they work, and eat their own bread."

This is not a condemnation of those who cannot find or acquire employment. It is admonishment of the faithful who have become fearful and apathetic in the face of something they do not understand — something that stares at them and confuses them, much like what they believed to be the end of days. Paul's Thessalonians had convinced themselves the return of Christ was so imminent that ordinary work no longer mattered. They stopped tending their trades, stopped keeping their shops, stopped showing up to the labor that fed their families, because they believed the world as they knew it was already ending. Paul does not comfort that fear. He corrects it. He tells them, plainly: the world has not ended, and the bread on your table still has to come from somewhere.

They, much like us today, faced what they did not understand — the loss of employment, the loss of work with their hands, due to changes they could not control. Like AI and factory machines putting our husbands and our sons out of work. Picture the machinist who spent twenty years learning the exact feel of a lathe, the specific sound it makes when the cut is right, and now stands in a break room watching a robotic arm run the same part a thousand times an hour without ever needing to learn a thing. Picture the woman who answered phones for a call center for fifteen years, who knew every regular customer by the sound of their voice, replaced overnight by a system that never gets tired and never needs a paycheck. That is not a hypothetical. That is somebody's father. That is somebody's son.

Consider how many people you know personally who have been displaced by technology from their employment, from their living — cast aside for simply the crime of being only human. How many of them are trying everything they know how to do to get back to work, and failing miserably. How many resumes have gone out into that silence. How many nights has someone in this room lain awake running the numbers on a bank account that keeps shrinking no matter how many applications go out the next morning.

This is the core concept that is upon the community to repair, to face. The community must be a shining beacon that guides their husbands and sons, their wives and daughters, their friends and loved ones, home — to prosperity, love, and happiness. Not a beacon that flickers on for an hour on a Sunday and goes dark the rest of the week. A beacon that stays lit through Tuesday afternoon phone calls and Thursday night doubts, until every last one of them finds their way back to solid ground.

---

## II. The Quiet Work of Your Own Hands

**1 Thessalonians 4:11-12**

> "And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you; that ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that ye may have lack of nothing."

Paul is not asking for silence here. He is asking for steadiness. "Study to be quiet" means make it your discipline, your practice, to stop the noise and the panic and put your hands back to work. Not loud, not desperate, not begging — quiet, honest, and diligent. There is a particular kind of dignity in a man who does not have to announce his effort, who simply gets up again after the last rejection letter and starts the next application, the next certification module, the next honest day's labor, without needing anyone to applaud him for it.

And notice what he says next: "that ye may walk honestly toward them that are without." That means the way we handle this — the way we retrain, the way we rebuild — is being watched. Every neighbor, every skeptic, and every person who does not believe the church has anything left to offer a man who just lost his job to a machine — they are "them that are without," and they are watching whether we help our own or whether we let them drown. They are watching whether faith produces anything real, or whether it is only words spoken into a microphone on a Sunday morning and forgotten by Monday.

This is why the Thessalonian Mandate Institute exists. Not to hand a man a check and send him away quiet and ashamed, but to put a certification in his hand — IBM, Google, Microsoft, and Fortinet, seven pathways deep — so that he can go back into the world and work with his own hands again, and lack nothing. So that the next time someone asks him what he does, he has an answer that does not require an apology.

---

## III. Even the Ant Knew Better

**Proverbs 6:6-11**

> "Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: which having no guide, overseer, or ruler, provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest."

Nobody had to teach the ant to prepare. Nobody had to threaten her into it, post a schedule on her wall, or send her a performance review. She looked at the season she was in and she moved, because the season itself was the instruction. That is the same instinct AI displacement is asking of every one of us right now — not permission to freeze in place while the ground shifts, but a season to prepare in, a summer that will not last forever and a harvest that will not wait for us to feel ready.

**Proverbs 14:23**

> "In all labour there is profit: but the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury."

We have talked this problem to death. Every panel, every op-ed, and every hand-wringing conversation about what AI is going to do to the American worker — that is talk, and more talk, and it has profited exactly no one sitting in these seats this morning who lost a job eleven months ago and still has not found the next one. Somebody has spent hours listening to economists on television debate the future of work while their own unemployment benefits ran out weeks ago. Labor produces profit. Talk only empties the pocket further. The Thessalonian Mandate Institute was not built to talk about the problem from a stage. It was built to put labor back in the hands of the displaced, one certification, one skill, one placement at a time.

---

## IV. Paul Made Tents

**Acts 18:3**

> "And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers."

Paul — the greatest missionary the church has ever produced, the man who carried the gospel across the known world and wrote half the New Testament — did not consider it beneath his calling to also be skilled with his hands in a trade. He preached in the synagogue on the Sabbath, and he made tents the rest of the week, cutting and stitching hide and canvas alongside Aquila and Priscilla, and one did not diminish the other. His trade funded his ministry so he never had to choose between feeding himself and preaching the word. It gave him standing in the marketplace, so the working people of Corinth and Ephesus saw him as one of their own before they ever heard him preach a sermon. It let him walk among them as a fellow laborer, not as someone above the sweat and calluses of an honest trade.

This is the model for every certification pathway the Institute offers. Learning cybersecurity, learning cloud infrastructure, and learning a trade for this new economy — none of that is a compromise of your calling. That is tentmaking. That is Paul's own example, applied to a generation facing a workforce none of us were prepared for, where the trade that funds your life might be one you learn at forty-five instead of nineteen, in a certification program instead of an apprenticeship, but the principle is exactly the same one Paul lived by two thousand years ago.

---

## V. A Future and a Hope

**Ecclesiastes 3:1**

> "To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven."

This season — the season of AI, of automation, of watching a machine do in seconds what took a man's father and grandfather a lifetime to master — this is a season. It is not the end of the story. It is a chapter, and chapters turn. The mill towns that lost their factories a generation ago did not stay empty forever, even when it felt at the time like nothing would ever come back. Seasons that feel endless from the inside are, from the outside, still just seasons.

**Jeremiah 29:11**

> "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end."

Consider who God was speaking to when He said this. He was not speaking to a comfortable people. He was speaking to an exiled people — a people who had lost their homes, their land, and their livelihood, dragged into a system that had not been built for them and did not care whether they survived it, scattered into a foreign country where nothing they knew how to do mattered anymore. And He told them: I have not forgotten you in this displacement. I have a future for you on the other side of it. Not a future that arrives instantly, not a future without the hard work of exile in between, but a future that is real and coming regardless.

That is the word for every husband and son in this room who has sent out three hundred applications and heard nothing back. That is the word for every wife and daughter watching the man they love lose himself in that silence, watching him stop believing his own hands are worth anything to anyone. This is a season of exile from the work you knew — not a verdict on your worth, and not the end of your story.

---

## VI. Be Not Weary

**2 Thessalonians 3:13**

> "But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing."

So here is the charge, and here is what the Thessalonian Mandate Institute stands ready to do. If you are in this room and you have been displaced — by AI, by automation, by a factory floor that no longer needs your hands — do not let that season make you weary in doing good, in trying, and in showing up one more time to learn one more skill, fill out one more application, sit through one more certification module even when the last three led nowhere.

And if you are in this room and you have not been displaced, then hear the charge that falls on you. Be the community. Be the beacon. Guide your husbands and your sons, your wives and your daughters, and your friends and your neighbors home — to prosperity, to love, and to happiness. That is the work the Institute was built to do. That is the work in front of us this morning, and it does not end when this service does.
SERMONEOF

This season — the season of AI, of automation, of watching a machine do in seconds what took a man's father and grandfather a lifetime to master — this is a season. It is not the end of the story. It is a chapter, and chapters turn. The mill towns that lost their factories a generation ago did not stay empty forever, even when it felt at the time like nothing would ever come back. Seasons that feel endless from the inside are, from the outside, still just seasons.

**Jeremiah 29:11**

> "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end."

Consider who God was speaking to when He said this. He was not speaking to a comfortable people. He was speaking to an exiled people — a people who had lost their homes, their land, and their livelihood, dragged into a system that had not been built for them and did not care whether they survived it, scattered into a foreign country where nothing they knew how to do mattered anymore. And He told them: I have not forgotten you in this displacement. I have a future for you on the other side of it. Not a future that arrives instantly, not a future without the hard work of exile in between, but a future that is real and coming regardless.

That is the word for every husband and son in this room who has sent out three hundred applications and heard nothing back. That is the word for every wife and daughter watching the man they love lose himself in that silence, watching him stop believing his own hands are worth anything to anyone. This is a season of exile from the work you knew — not a verdict on your worth, and not the end of your story.

---

## VI. Be Not Weary

**2 Thessalonians 3:13**

> "But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing."

So here is the charge, and here is what the Thessalonian Mandate Institute stands ready to do. If you are in this room and you have been displaced — by AI, by automation, by a factory floor that no longer needs your hands — do not let that season make you weary in doing good, in trying, and in showing up one more time to learn one more skill, fill out one more application, sit through one more certification module even when the last three led nowhere.

And if you are in this room and you have not been displaced, then hear the charge that falls on you. Be the community. Be the beacon. Guide your husbands and your sons, your wives and your daughters, and your friends and your neighbors home — to prosperity, to love, and to happiness. That is the work the Institute was built to do. That is the work in front of us this morning, and it does not end when this service does.
